stimuli.text: A solid insulating sphere of radius R = 0.12 m has a total charge Q = +7 nC distributed uniformly throughout its volume.
An initially uncharged 3 µF capacitor, a 120 kΩ resistor, an ideal 7 V battery and an open switch are connected in series. The switch is closed at t = 0.
Students measure the resistance of different lengths of a wire with a diameter of 0.5 mm, using a battery, an ammeter and a voltmeter.

A conducting rod of mass 0.9 kg and length 0.9 m slides without friction on horizontal rails connected by a 7 Ω resistor. A uniform 1 T magnetic field points vertically through the rails. The rod is given an initial speed of 3 m/s and then released.

questions.stem: A 9 µF capacitor is in parallel with a series combination of 10 µF and 8 µF. What is the equivalent capacitance?

options.why: Correct. Capacitors add in parallel; reciprocals add in series.
The series and parallel rules are swapped (they are the reverse of resistors).
Not all the capacitors are in series.
Not all the capacitors are in parallel.

questions.stem: An electron starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of 1000 V. What is its final speed? ($$m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}$$ kg)
A 0.47 H inductor carries 2 A. How much energy is stored in its magnetic field?
The current in a wire is $$I(t) = 8t$$ A. How much charge passes a point from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 4$$ s?
A solenoid 0.2 m long has 200 turns and carries 4 A. What is the magnetic field inside it?

options.why: That resembles a wire's field; use B = μ₀nI.
Correct. B = μ₀nI with n = N/L.

questions.stem: A 28 µF capacitor is charged to 60 V. How much energy does it store?
A flat circular coil of 2 turns and radius 0.18 m carries 6 A. What is the field at its center?

options.why: That is a straight wire's field.

questions.stem: A proton moves at $$8 \times 10^{5}$$ m/s perpendicular to a uniform 0.04 T magnetic field. What is the radius of its path?

options.why: Correct. qvB = mv²/r, so r = mv/(qB).

questions.stem: Point P is 0.6 m from a +9 µC charge and 0.6 m from a −2 µC charge. What is the electric potential at P?

options.why: Correct. Potential is a scalar: add kq/r with signs.
The negative charge contributes negative potential.

questions.stem: A wire 14 m long has a diameter of 1.4 mm and resistivity $$1.7 \times 10^{-8}$$ Ω·m. What is its resistance?

options.why: Correct. R = ρL/A with A = π(d/2)².

questions.stem: Two parallel plates 0.06 m apart have a potential difference of 140 V. What is the field between them?

options.why: Correct. In a uniform field, E = ΔV/d.

questions.stem: A battery with emf 6 V and internal resistance 0.7 Ω is connected to a 13 Ω resistor. What is the current?

options.why: Correct. I = ε/(R + r); V = ε − Ir.

questions.stem: Two identical small conducting spheres carry 3 µC and 0 µC. They are touched together and separated. What is the charge on each?

options.why: Correct. Identical conductors share the total charge equally.
The total is shared between two spheres.

questions.explanation: Total 3 µC, split equally: 1.5 µC each.

questions.stem: An electron starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of 150 V. What is its final speed? ($$m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}$$ kg)
How much work must an external agent do to move a +6 µC charge slowly from a point at -50 V to a point at 119 V?
A uniform field of 600 N/C passes through a flat 0.7 m² surface whose normal makes 60° with the field. What is the flux through the surface?

options.why: θ is measured from the normal, so use cos θ.

questions.stem: A 0.5 m wire carrying 17 A makes a 30° angle with a uniform 0.3 T magnetic field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on it?

options.why: Use sin θ, from the cross product.

questions.stem: A battery with emf 24 V and internal resistance 0.9 Ω is connected to a 5 Ω resistor. What is the current?

options.why: Correct. I = ε/(R + r); V = ε − Ir.

questions.stem: A 26 Ω resistor is connected across 90 V. What power does it dissipate?
Two point charges of 5 µC and −5 µC are 0.37 m apart. What is the magnitude of the force between them?
A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.05 m² separated by 8 mm, filled with a dielectric of κ = 5. What is its capacitance?
A long straight wire carries a uniform charge of 2 µC/m. What is the field 0.37 m from it?

options.why: A line charge's field falls off as 1/r.
Correct. E = λ/(2πε₀r), from Gauss's law with a cylinder.

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.19 m² separated by 1 mm of air. What is its capacitance?
A 110-turn coil of area 0.08 m² is perpendicular to a magnetic field that changes by 0.9 T in 0.9 s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf?

options.why: Multiply by the number of turns.

questions.stem: An LC circuit has a 36 mH inductor and a 39 µF capacitor. What is its angular frequency ω of oscillation?
A 9 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 7 Ω and 3 Ω, connected to an ideal 20 V battery. What is the equivalent resistance?

options.why: Correct. Reduce the parallel pair, add the series resistor, then work back.
R₂ and R₃ are in parallel.

questions.stem: Charges of 1 µC, 3 µC, -3 µC sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle with sides 0.5 m. What is the system's electric potential energy?

options.why: Keep the signs of the charges.
Correct. Add kqᵢqⱼ/r for all three pairs.

questions.stem: A long straight wire carries 29 A. What is the magnetic field 0.19 m from it?

options.why: That is the field at the center of a loop.
A long wire's field falls off as 1/r.

questions.stem: A conducting sphere of radius 1 cm carrying 32 nC is connected by a long thin wire to an uncharged conducting sphere of radius 7 cm far away. What charge ends up on the smaller sphere?

options.why: Equal potential gives Q ∝ R, not R².
Correct. Connected spheres reach equal potential, so Q ∝ R.
That is the larger sphere's charge.

questions.explanation: kQ₁/R₁ = kQ₂/R₂ with Q₁ + Q₂ = 32: Q₁ = 4 nC.

questions.stem: A ring of radius 0.07 m carries 5 µC spread uniformly. What is the field magnitude on its axis 0.25 m from the center?

options.why: Only the axial components add; the others cancel.
The charge is not at the center.

questions.stem: A solid insulating sphere of radius 0.2 m has 3 µC distributed uniformly through its volume. What is the field magnitude 0.12 m from its center?

options.why: Correct. Inside, the enclosed charge is Q(r/R)³, so E = kQr/R³.
That is the field at the surface.
Only the charge inside radius r counts.

questions.stem: A charge of +9q is at $$x = 0$$ and a charge of +q is at $$x = 7$$ m. At what point between them is the electric field zero?

options.why: The zero point is closer to the smaller charge.
Compare r², so take square roots.

questions.stem: An ideal 18 V battery is connected at $$t = 0$$ to a 1 Ω resistor and a 0.9 H inductor in series. What is the current at $$t = 1.8$$ s?

options.why: Correct. τ = L/R = 0.9 s; I = (ε/R)(1 − e^(−t/τ)).
The current has not reached its final value.

questions.stem: A 8 µF capacitor starts uncharged and is charged through a 60 kΩ resistor by a 12 V battery. What is the capacitor's voltage after 0.24 s?

options.why: Convert kΩ and µF to Ω and F.
That is the charging resistor's voltage.
Correct. τ = RC = 0.48 s; V = ε(1 − e^(−t/τ)).
The change is exponential, not linear.

questions.stem: Charges of +3 µC and +6 µC are 1 m apart. What is the magnitude of the electric field at the midpoint between them?

options.why: Correct. Like charges' fields point in opposite directions at the midpoint: subtract.
Check the directions of the two fields at the midpoint.
The distance is d/2, so r² = d²/4.
Each charge is d/2 from the midpoint.

questions.explanation: Each field is k q/(d/2)²: 1.08 \times 10^{5} and 2.16 \times 10^{5} N/C, opposite, giving 1.08 \times 10^{5} N/C.

questions.stem: A single loop contains a 12 V battery and a 1 V battery connected so their emfs oppose each other, plus resistors of 1 Ω and 7 Ω. What is the current?

options.why: Both resistors are in the loop.
Correct. Loop rule: ε₁ − ε₂ − I(R₁ + R₂) = 0.

questions.stem: Two long parallel wires 0.02 m apart carry 18 A and 13 A in the same direction. What is the force per meter between them?

options.why: Correct. F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd); parallel currents attract.
Parallel currents attract; antiparallel currents repel.
The force per length falls off as 1/d.

questions.stem: The electric potential along the x-axis is $$V(x) = 70x^2$$ V. What is the x-component of the electric field at $$x = 1$$ m?
A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and remains connected to the battery. A dielectric with κ = 2 is inserted to fill the gap. What happens to the capacitor's charge?

options.why: Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.
Inserting the dielectric changes the capacitance.
Decide first whether Q or V is held fixed.
Correct. With the battery connected, V is fixed and C rises by κ.

questions.explanation: C becomes κC. V fixed: Q = CV and U = ½CV² rise by κ.

questions.stem: A rectangular loop of length 0.2 m lies in the plane of a long straight wire carrying 14 A, parallel to it. Its near and far sides are 0.08 m and 0.17 m from the wire. What is the magnetic flux through the loop?

options.why: The field is not uniform across the loop.

parts.prompt: Using Gauss's law, derive expressions for the electric field magnitude inside (r < R) and outside (r > R) the sphere.

rubric.criterion: Spherical Gaussian surface; enclosed charge inside is Q(r/R)³.

parts.prompt: Calculate the field magnitude at r = 0.06 m and at r = 0.24 m.
Sketch (describe) a graph of E versus r from 0 to 3R.

rubric.criterion: Linear increase from 0 to a maximum at R, then 1/r² decrease.
rubric.example: Peak value kQ/R² = 4370 N/C at r = R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the electric potential at the surface and at the center (V = 0 at infinity).

rubric.criterion: Center potential by integrating the inside field.

parts.prompt: Write the loop equation for the circuit and solve it to find q(t).
Calculate the time constant, the initial current and the final charge on the capacitor.
Sketch (describe) graphs of the capacitor's voltage and the current versus time.

rubric.criterion: Capacitor voltage rises from 0 toward ε, concave down.
Current decays exponentially from I₀ toward 0.
rubric.example: About 37% of I₀ at t = τ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the energy stored in the capacitor after a long time, and compare it with the energy supplied by the battery.

rubric.criterion: The battery supplies Qε, twice as much; half is dissipated in the resistor.

parts.prompt: Describe (draw) how the ammeter and voltmeter should be connected, and how R is determined.

rubric.criterion: Ammeter in series with the wire; voltmeter in parallel across it.
Keep the current small or brief so the wire does not heat up.

parts.prompt: Plot (describe) R versus L and draw a best-fit line. Calculate its slope.
Use the slope to calculate the resistivity of the wire.

rubric.criterion: Uses slope = ρ/A with A = π(d/2)².

parts.prompt: The students then use a wire of the same material with twice the diameter. Predict the new slope of R versus L and explain.

rubric.criterion: The slope becomes one quarter as large because the area quadruples.

questions.title: A sliding rod in a magnetic field

parts.prompt: Describe qualitatively how the rod's speed changes after it is released, and explain using Lenz's law.

rubric.criterion: The rod slows down, approaching zero.
rubric.example: Its speed decreases ever more slowly.

rubric.criterion: The induced current produces a magnetic force opposing the motion (Lenz's law).
rubric.example: The force opposes the change in flux.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the magnetic force on the rod in terms of B, L, v and R.

rubric.criterion: Uses ε = BLv and I = ε/R.

parts.prompt: Write and solve a differential equation for v(t).
Calculate the initial current, and explain where the rod's initial kinetic energy ends up.

rubric.criterion: All of the kinetic energy is dissipated as thermal energy in the resistor.
